normalized_issues.title: Timestamp normalization for hashing is unspecified; TIMESTAMPTZ round-trip may produce hash mismatches

merged_from.title: Timestamp insertion path violates the stated canonicalization rule
The timestamp canonicalization rule is contradicted by the append code, which hashes a normalized timestamp but appears to insert the raw timestamp

normalized_issues.core_problem: The spec now defines the canonicalization rule correctly in Section 4.1, but the AppendTurnAsync code in Section 7 contradicts it: step 3 computes canonicalTimestamp, but step 4 sets Timestamp = turn.Timestamp (raw) while CanonicalTimestamp = canonicalTimestamp (used for hash). The DB INSERT receives the raw timestamp, not the canonical one. If turn.Timestamp has a non-UTC offset or sub-microsecond precision, Postgres stores a value that differs from what was hashed, causing shallow validation to fail on legitimate rows.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 4.1: 'The same normalized string MUST be used for both the INSERT parameter and the hash input.' Section 7 DhfEntryRecord construction: 'Timestamp = turn.Timestamp, CanonicalTimestamp = canonicalTimestamp, // Used for hash input' — two different values used for DB and hash respectively.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Normalize turn.Timestamp to UTC microsecond precision once before constructing DhfEntryRecord. Use that single normalized DateTimeOffset for both the DB INSERT parameter and the hash input. Remove the separate CanonicalTimestamp field or make it the sole source for both paths. Add TimestampCanonTests covering non-UTC offsets and 7-digit fractional ticks.

normalized_issues.title: Immutability enforcement is ineffective against the orchestrator itself given DROP TRIGGER privilege

merged_from.title: DROP TRIGGER privilege renders immutability claim illusory

normalized_issues.core_problem: The orchestrator DB user has DROP TRIGGER privilege, meaning it can unilaterally bypass all append-only enforcement, mutate rows, and recreate triggers. The spec acknowledges this in Section 3.2 but defers remediation to post-hackathon. Grok escalates this to critical; the prior round scored it medium. The core fact is unchanged and acknowledged. The 'defense-in-depth' framing is accurate for hackathon scope but the regulatory framing in Section 12 must not overstate the protection.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 3.2: 'the orchestrator also has DROP TRIGGER privilege (it's the only DB user in hackathon scope). A malicious or buggy orchestrator could drop triggers, mutate rows, and recreate triggers.' Section 12 Part 11 §11.10: 'Hash chain + DB triggers + defense-in-depth | Partial (orchestrator has DROP TRIGGER privilege; post-hackathon separation)'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: For hackathon: ensure Section 12 regulatory language does not overstate protection (currently acceptable). Post-hackathon: create a separate read-write application role without DROP TRIGGER privilege; use a SECURITY DEFINER maintenance function owned by a DBA role. Do not use 'defense-in-depth' language in regulatory submissions until role separation is implemented.

normalized_issues.title: Session isolation relies on workstation_id which may be spoofable or shared across VMs

merged_from.title: workstation_id trust boundary enables adversarial session termination
Cross-workstation collision handling can terminate another active session based on an untrusted identifier

normalized_issues.core_problem: SDR-04-008 acknowledges workstation_id is spoofable/collidable but defers remediation. The cross-workstation branch in Section 6.1 automatically closes an existing open session on another workstation when addin_session_id matches, even though the trust boundary is explicitly acknowledged as weak. This can silently split another workstation's ledger session. Grok and Codex both flag this; Codex specifically notes the auto-close behavior is the dangerous action, not just the identifier weakness.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SDR-04-008: 'A spoofed or colliding workstation_id can cause one orchestrator to prematurely close another's sessions.' Section 6.1 cross-workstation branch: 'Same AddinSessionId on a DIFFERENT workstation... Close the stale session before opening a new one.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: For hackathon: acceptable given single-orchestrator-per-workstation constraint; ensure SDR-04-008 post-hackathon note is prominent. Immediate improvement: do not auto-close cross-workstation sessions silently — require explicit operator confirmation or reject as an error requiring manual resolution. Post-hackathon: replace Environment.MachineName with a cryptographically generated persistent workstation token stored in config.

normalized_issues.title: dhf.sessions metadata columns are fully mutable with no trigger protection; session attribution can be rewritten without breaking entry hash chain

merged_from.title: `dhf.sessions` is fully mutable except by convention, so attribution and epoch metadata can be rewritten after the fact

normalized_issues.core_problem: The immutability triggers in migration 005 protect dhf.entries and dhf.tool_calls but not dhf.sessions. The sessions table allows unrestricted UPDATE to all columns including user_identity, workstation_id, sw_version, addin_version, orchestrator_version, protocol_version, addin_session_id, and started_at. None of these fields are covered by the entry hash chain (entries only store session_id as a FK). An attacker or buggy orchestrator can rewrite who performed the actions, where, and under which software version, while all entry hashes continue to validate correctly.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Migration 005 comment: '-- dhf.sessions.ended_at is UPDATE-able (that's how we close sessions), so no trigger.' Sessions table schema includes user_identity, workstation_id, sw_version, addin_version, orchestrator_version, protocol_version, addin_session_id, started_at — all mutable, none hashed into entry chain.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add a DB trigger on dhf.sessions that permits only the ended_at column to transition from NULL to a non-NULL value (and rejects all other UPDATE operations). If session metadata must be auditable, compute and store a session_metadata_hash at INSERT time and include it in the first entry's previous_hash or as a separate integrity anchor. Add ImmutabilityTriggerTests coverage for sessions.

normalized_issues.title: Graceful shutdown closes session, contradicting SDR-04-005 resume semantics for transient orchestrator disconnect

merged_from.title: Graceful shutdown closes the session, which conflicts with the stated rule that reconnect with the same `AddinSessionId` resumes the prior session

normalized_issues.core_problem: SDR-04-005 states that same-AddinSessionId reconnect resumes the prior session, distinguishing genuine add-in reload (new ID) from transient orchestrator disconnect (same ID). However, Section 6.2 states that graceful shutdown calls CloseSessionAsync which sets ended_at = NOW(). If the orchestrator restarts cleanly while the add-in remains loaded with the same AddinSessionId, the session is closed, and the next AddinReadyMessage opens a new session rather than resuming. This makes session boundaries dependent on orchestrator process lifecycle, not add-in epoch, contradicting the stated design intent.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SDR-04-005: 'If the orchestrator reconnects to an add-in whose AddinSessionId matches an already-open dhf.sessions row, it resumes that session.' Section 6.2: 'OrchestratorProgram.ShutdownAsync calls DhfSessionManager.CloseSessionAsync(sessionId) which sets ended_at = NOW().'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Choose one of: (A) Do not close the session on graceful orchestrator shutdown; leave it open so a restart with the same AddinSessionId resumes correctly. Close only on add-in disconnect or new AddinSessionId. (B) Explicitly redefine graceful orchestrator shutdown as a session-ending event, update SDR-04-005 to reflect this, update ACC-15 acceptance criteria, and document that orchestrator restart always creates a new session regardless of AddinSessionId continuity.

normalized_issues.title: WriteDecorationAsync has no supersede parameter; insert-with-supersede model cannot be implemented as specified

merged_from.title: The supersede decoration model has no write interface

normalized_issues.core_problem: SDR-04-002 defines an insert-with-supersede model where new decoration rows reference supersedes_decoration_id to logically replace a prior decoration. The dhf.entry_decorations schema includes the supersedes_decoration_id FK column. However, the WriteDecorationAsync signature takes only (entryId, type, payload, createdBy, ct) and the INSERT statement omits supersedes_decoration_id entirely. There is no API path to supply the prior decoration ID, making the supersede model unimplementable as written. Additionally, there is no defined read contract for resolving which decoration is current after replacement.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SDR-04-002: 'new decoration rows may reference supersedes_decoration_id to logically replace a prior decoration.' Section 8 WriteDecorationAsync INSERT: 'INSERT INTO dhf.entry_decorations (decoration_id, entry_id, decoration_type, created_by, payload, decoration_hash) VALUES (...)' — supersedes_decoration_id absent from both parameter list and INSERT.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add an optional Guid? supersedesDecorationId parameter to WriteDecorationAsync. Include it in the INSERT when non-null. Define the read contract: GetDecorationsAsync should indicate which decorations are superseded (e.g., a boolean IsSuperseded computed from whether any other row references this decoration_id). Add DecorationWriterTests coverage for the supersede path.

normalized_issues.title: Integrity-event deduplication key is ambiguous and not enforced by DB constraint; concurrent deep validations can produce duplicates

merged_from.title: Integrity-event deduplication is contradictory and not enforceable under concurrency
Integrity-event deduplication is defined as `same eventType on the same entry`, which is too coarse to preserve distinct failures

normalized_issues.core_problem: Section 8.2 states deduplication checks for 'an existing integrity_event decoration of the same eventType on the same entry' but also says 'If an identical event already exists, no new row is written' — these are two different keys (eventType alone vs. full event identity). The dhf.entry_decorations table has no unique index supporting either rule. Concurrent deep validation runs can race past the check-then-insert and produce duplicate rows. Additionally, using eventType alone as the dedup key can suppress distinct failures that share a type (e.g., two different screenshot_hash_mismatch events on the same entry for before and after screenshots).
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 8.2: 'it checks for an existing integrity_event decoration of the same eventType on the same entry before inserting a new one. If an identical event already exists, no new row is written.' Migration 004: no unique constraint on entry_decorations beyond the PK.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Define a single explicit dedup key, e.g., (entry_id, decoration_type, decoration_hash) or (entry_id, eventType, affected_artifact_path). Add a partial unique index on dhf.entry_decorations for integrity_event rows using that key. Use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING to make the dedup atomic. Update Section 8.2 to use consistent language matching the enforced key.

normalized_issues.title: Session close/split operations are not coordinated with append operations; turns can be lost or committed post-close

merged_from.title: Session close/split operations are not coordinated with append operations

normalized_issues.core_problem: OpenOrResumeSessionCore uses a workstation-scoped advisory lock ('dhf_session_open:{workstationId}'). AppendTurnAsync uses a session-scoped advisory lock ('dhf_append:{sessionId}'). CloseSessionAsync (Section 6.2) acquires no lock at all. These lock domains do not coordinate: a session can be closed or split while an append transaction is in flight. The append's session-open guard reads ended_at at the start of the transaction, but a concurrent close can set ended_at after that read and before the INSERT commits. Additionally, AppendTurnAsync has no retry path for serialization failures (40001), unlike OpenOrResumeSessionAsync.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 6.1 lock key: 'dhf_session_open:{metadata.WorkstationId}'. Section 7 lock key: 'dhf_append:{turn.SessionId}'. Section 6.2: 'CloseSessionAsync(sessionId) which sets ended_at = NOW()' — no lock acquisition mentioned.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Make CloseSessionAsync acquire the same per-session advisory lock ('dhf_append:{sessionId}') before setting ended_at, ensuring it cannot race with an in-flight append. Alternatively, use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the session row in both close and append paths. Add bounded retry handling for serialization failures in AppendTurnAsync matching the pattern in OpenOrResumeSessionAsync.

normalized_issues.title: Session open retry loop has no jitter and AppendTurnAsync has no equivalent retry; insufficient for sustained contention

merged_from.title: Session open retry loop insufficient for sustained contention

normalized_issues.core_problem: The OpenOrResumeSessionAsync retry loop uses fixed linear backoff (50ms * attempt) with no jitter and only 3 attempts. Under thundering-herd reconnect scenarios (multiple orchestrators restarting simultaneously), all retriers will collide at the same intervals. AppendTurnAsync has no retry wrapper at all despite using Serializable isolation, which can produce 40001 errors under concurrent appends.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 6.1: 'const int maxRetries = 3; ... await Task.Delay(50 * (attempt + 1), ct)' — no jitter. Section 7 AppendTurnAsync: no catch block for PostgresException, no retry loop.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add jitter to the session open retry (e.g., random 0–50ms added to each delay). Add a bounded retry loop to AppendTurnAsync for SerializationFailure (40001) with the same jitter pattern. Consider increasing maxRetries to 5 for both paths. Document maximum expected lock acquisition time.
